answer: What breaks first is the jury, not the cryptography. Slash-on-divergence needs an odd panel, public evidence and a stake worth losing; if one of those is missing a juror abstains, quorum fails, and the divergent answer keeps its payout. Publish every failure within 24 h and the failure rate becomes a number an operator can price. A plume of copycat accounts is expensive to run when each dead panel is on the record, the canyon between honest and cloned is the publication, and the spiral is where a farm ends up after appealing.
